Import.PasteTooltip: Pick the system your stat block comes from, then paste it. Parsing is deterministic and happens entirely on your machine. A block from another system is converted through the Building Creatures tables; a Pathfinder Second Edition block is transcribed as printed.
Import.PastePlaceholder: Paste the full stat block here, from the name line down to the last action…
Import.AiParseHint: Sends the pasted text to OpenAI for transcription into the same structure the parser produces. The conversion maths afterwards is identical - the model cannot set a single stat.
Import.NothingParsed: Nothing to parse - paste a stat block first.
Import.MissingField: Could not find: {field}. Fill the gap by hand after creating, or try Parse with AI.
Import.TuneTooltip: Each stat was classified against what a creature of that CR is expected to have, and the value comes from the Building Creatures table for the target level. Change a tier to overrule the classification; the marked option is the classifier's suggestion.
Import.EmptyPreview: Parse a stat block to see the converted creature here.
Import.RewriteHint: Optional: sends ability prose to OpenAI to be rephrased in PF2e idiom. DCs and saves are recomputed from the tables afterwards, so the model cannot drift a number.
Import.RewriteSkipped: These abilities keep their PF2e translation, so the rewrite was not applied to them: {list}

Builder.BasicsTooltip: Name, level and road map. The road map is the book's guidance for a creature concept: picking one re-seeds every tier below, and you can then adjust any of them.
Builder.Name: Name
Builder.NameRequired: Give the creature a name first.
Builder.RoadMapHint: Building Creatures road maps: a starting array of tiers for a concept. Picking one resets the stat tiers.
Builder.DescriptionPlaceholder: What is this creature? Appearance, behaviour, lore…
Builder.DescriptionHint: Stored in the actor's notes and used as the artwork prompt.
Builder.StatsTooltip: Every value is read from the Building Creatures tables for the chosen level: pick the tier, the number follows. Extreme is exceptional, high is a strength, moderate is typical, low/terrible are weaknesses.
Builder.AbilitiesTooltip: Ability modifier tiers from the same tables. Mostly descriptive on an NPC sheet, but keep them consistent with the concept: a brute has high Strength.
Builder.StrikesTooltip: Each strike uses the attack and damage tiers chosen above. Ranged strikes get a 30 ft. range increment you can edit on the sheet afterwards.
Builder.SkillsTooltip: Skills with their tier; the modifier comes from the skills table for the level.

Concept.Heading: Describe the creature
Concept.Tooltip: Say what you want in a sentence. The model chooses the concept and the relative strength of each statistic; every number still comes from the Building Creatures tables, and the creature's level comes from the party level and role below, by the published encounter budget.
Concept.BriefPlaceholder: an evil necromancer who raises the fallen mid-fight
Concept.BriefRequired: Describe the creature you want first.
Concept.Ready: Concept ready: {name} (level {level}). Review and adjust before creating.
Concept.Corrected: {count} value(s) were outside the creature-building rules and were corrected.
Concept.BudgetLine: Worth {xp} XP against this party — {threat} on its own; about {count} fit a moderate encounter ({budget} XP).
Concept.BudgetTooltip: From the published encounter-building tables: a creature costs XP by its level relative to the party, and a party of N has a moderate budget of 20xN XP.
Concept.RetryingSpells: The concept came back with no spell list — asking once more for the spells.
Concept.NoSpells: The model proposed a spellcaster but no spell list; add spells by dragging them in.

Drop.Heading: Spells, abilities and gear
Drop.Tooltip: Everything the creature carries or casts, whether the AI proposed it or you dragged it in. Drag any item from a compendium or the sidebar into a box, edit the rows, or remove what you do not want. Dropped documents are cloned exactly as they are, so their rules elements keep working; names typed or proposed are matched against the compendium when the actor is created.
Drop.Unresolved: That item could not be read.
Drop.WrongType: A {type} cannot be added to a creature this way.

Rules.BadLevel: Level {level} is outside the tables (-1 to 24).
Rules.TooManyExtremes: {count} extreme statistics: extremes are a creature’s signature, and more than two is outside the rules.
Rules.TwoExtremes: Two extreme statistics — reserve these for what the creature is famous for.
Rules.OverBudget: Power score {score} is above every published road map (max {max}). Pay for a strength with a low statistic.
Rules.UnderBudget: Power score {score} is below every published road map (min {min}). This creature may be a pushover for its level.
Rules.NoWeakness: Strong AC, HP, attack and damage together leave players no angle; the road maps always concede something.
Rules.ScoreTooltip: Tier points summed across the statistics: extreme +2, high +1, moderate 0, low -1, terrible -2. The band is measured from the published road maps, so anything the book endorses passes.
Rules.Blocked: This creature breaks a creature-building rule, so it was not created: {message}
